name: Synthetic Test State

program.agency: None. ZZ is a synthetic jurisdiction for engine tests.

rules.summary: A provider may not bill the survivor for any part of the forensic exam.
rules.quote: A health care provider shall not bill a victim for any part of a sexual assault forensic examination.

rules.summary: The state examination fund pays for the forensic exam.
rules.quote: The state examination fund pays the full cost of a sexual assault forensic examination.

params.payer: County, for injury treatment within 72 hours

rules.summary: The county pays for injury treatment given within 72 hours; this is medical care, not the exam.
rules.quote: The county pays for treatment of physical injuries given within 72 hours after the victim first arrives for care.

rules.summary: The total award is capped at $25,000.
rules.quote: The total award on a claim shall not exceed $25,000.

rules.summary: No award under the title may exceed $30,000.
rules.quote: No award under any program in this title shall exceed $30,000.

rules.summary: Counseling is paid at up to $80 per session, for up to 40 sessions.
rules.quote: Counseling is reimbursed at not more than $80 per session, for up to 40 sessions.

rules.summary: Counseling on one claim is capped at $3,000.
rules.quote: Counseling costs on a claim shall not exceed $3,000.

rules.summary: Lost wages are paid at up to $400 per week.
rules.quote: Lost wages are paid at not more than $400 per week.

rules.summary: Relocation is capped at $2,000.
rules.quote: Relocation costs shall not exceed $2,000.

rules.summary: Residential security is capped at $1,000 per residence.
rules.quote: Residential security costs shall not exceed $1,000 per residence.

rules.summary: Transportation to treatment is paid at $0.50 per mile.
rules.quote: Transportation to treatment is reimbursed at $0.50 per mile.

rules.summary: Temporary housing is covered for up to 30 days.
rules.quote: Temporary housing is covered for up to 30 days.

rules.summary: Crime scene cleanup is capped at $5,000 per crime scene.
rules.quote: Crime scene cleanup shall not exceed $5,000 per crime scene.

rules.summary: Peer counseling is paid up to $15 an hour.
rules.quote: Counseling by a peer counselor is reimbursed at not more than $15 per hour.

rules.summary: Medical expenses are covered.
rules.quote: The program may pay reasonable medical expenses.

rules.summary: Counseling is covered.
rules.quote: The program may pay for counseling.

rules.summary: Lost wages are covered.
rules.quote: The program may pay lost wages.

rules.summary: Transportation to treatment is covered.
rules.quote: The program may pay for transportation to treatment.

rules.summary: Relocation is covered.
rules.quote: The program may pay relocation costs.

rules.summary: Prescriptions are covered.
rules.quote: The program may pay for prescriptions.

rules.summary: Dental costs are covered.
rules.quote: The program may pay dental costs.

rules.summary: Childcare is covered.
rules.quote: The program may pay childcare costs.

rules.summary: Replacement eyeglasses are covered.
rules.quote: The program may pay for replacement eyeglasses.

rules.summary: Lost or damaged personal property is not covered.
rules.quote: The program shall not pay for lost or damaged personal property.

rules.summary: Pain and suffering is not covered.
rules.quote: The program shall not pay for pain and suffering.

rules.summary: Childcare is not covered for an adult claimant.
rules.quote: The program shall not pay childcare costs for a claimant who is an adult.

rules.summary: File within 3 years of the crime.
rules.quote: A claim shall be filed within 3 years after the crime.

rules.summary: File within 180 days of discovering the injury.
rules.quote: A claim shall be filed within 180 days after the victim discovers the injury.

rules.summary: A victim who was a minor may file within 10 years after turning eighteen.
rules.quote: A victim who was a minor may file within 10 years after turning eighteen.

rules.summary: The board may extend the deadline for good cause.
rules.quote: The board may extend a filing deadline for good cause.

rules.summary: A sexual assault claim can be filed up to 2 years after the police report.
rules.quote: A claim based on a sexual assault may be filed within 2 years after the crime is reported to law enforcement.

rules.summary: Report to law enforcement within 30 days, unless the survivor had a forensic exam.
rules.quote: The crime shall be reported to law enforcement within 30 days, unless the victim had a sexual assault forensic examination.

rules.summary: No police report is needed to get a forensic exam.
rules.quote: A victim does not need to report to law enforcement to receive a forensic examination.

rules.summary: A claim needs at least $100 of loss, except for a victim of sexual assault.
rules.quote: A claim requires an out-of-pocket loss of at least $100, which does not apply to a victim of sexual assault.

rules.summary: Lost wages count after 5 missed working days.
rules.quote: Lost wages are paid only when the victim misses at least 5 working days.

rules.summary: The program pays after insurance and other sources.
rules.quote: The program pays only after insurance and other collateral sources.

rules.summary: An award may be reduced for the victim's conduct (shown as information only).
rules.quote: An award may be reduced if the victim's conduct contributed to the injury.

rules.summary: An emergency award of up to $1,000 is available.
rules.quote: The board may grant an emergency award of up to $1,000.

rules.summary: Sexual assault is a covered crime.
rules.quote: Sexual assault is a crime covered by this title.

params.rule: Residents, and anyone injured by a crime in ZZ

rules.summary: Residents and people hurt by a crime in ZZ may apply.
rules.quote: Residents of ZZ and people injured by a crime in ZZ may apply.

coverage.notes: Synthetic fixture. Every category appears at least once, with edge cases for each engine step.

researcher_notes: Synthetic jurisdiction for refengine tests and the differential test. Not a real program; the quotes were written for testing and are not law.
